etymology: Named for the Soviet reply to every complaint: "and what about…?"
committed_when: A specific question has been asked that the speaker would rather not answer.
tell: The reply begins with "what about" and never returns to the question.
counter: Say that the other case can be discussed after this one, and repeat the question. The order of questions is a fair thing to insist on.
senses: Deflecting a question by raising a different grievance, so the original subject never gets answered.
It works because there is always another grievance. The move does not have to be false - it only has to be more interesting than the question being asked.
example: *"What about the crime in your city?"* The question was about a contract. Both can be answered; only one was asked.

confused_with.tell: Tu quoque answers a charge with a charge against the accuser; whataboutism raises any third subject at all.
